title: fix(app-shell): a declared flow action's button starts its flow through the action door (objectui#12037)
body:
Fixes #12037

Clause-②: no

Built on triage ruling B (card comment `6077692839`): a flow click goes through the action door exactly when it names a declared flow action; every other flow start stays on the trigger route. Ruling A landed in objectstack-ai/objectstack#22424. Implemented by session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MgfduSkFrfM3eorB3UGfAU` (seat `domain:ui#2`).

## What changes

Both console flow-launch handlers used to start every flow through `POST /api/v1/automation/:flow/trigger`: `flowHandler` in `useConsoleActionRuntime` (list, page and root runtime) and `flowHandler` in `RecordDetailView`. That route starts a flow by name, so a declared flow action's own server gates never ran for the click. Those gates are its `requiredPermissions` (ADR-0066 D4, whose console half only hides the button), its activation switch, its param contract and the caller-scoped load of its subject record.

- **The route rule** lives in one module-internal launcher, `launchConsoleFlow` in the new `packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowLaunch.ts`, which both handlers call. A click goes through `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action` exactly when `findDeclaredFlowAction` finds, in the object metadata the console already holds, an action of the click's `name` on the click's object with `type: 'flow'` and the same `target`. Otherwise the click stays on the trigger route. Both handlers' docblocks record why: an undeclared flow start has no action gate to apply, and ruling A's elevation refusal already holds on the trigger route. Those starts are an inline page button with no or a non-matching `name`, and a dashboard header's synthesized `name: actionUrl`.
- **Who owns the door's exchange.** The `/actions` request is built by core's `createServerActionHandler` (name-only identity, `{ recordId, params }`, `_rowRecord` stripped), so app-shell still names that route nowhere (`actions-envelope.ratchet.test.ts` stays green, unedited). The answer is the flow's `AutomationResult`, read by `interpretFlowResponse` / `judgeFlowLaunch` through an injected transport. So a paused screen still opens `FlowRunner`, a refused end still opens the Close-only notice, and `FLOW_FAILED` still prefers the author's `errorMessage`. Core's own `interpretActionResponse` has none of those arms.
- **Ride-along, related-list toolbar.** `RecordDetailView`'s flow path no longer hands the parent page's record id to a child object's action that carries no row. A related list's toolbar flow action is now an object-level start; a row action still addresses the child row.
- **Docs.** In `content/docs/guide/architecture-overview.md`, the *Supported Action Types* `flow` row now says what the type does and which endpoint each kind of click uses.
- `flow-envelope.ratchet.test.ts` names the callers that are true now: `utils/flowLaunch.ts` (launch) and `views/FlowRunner.tsx` (resume). It also pins that both handlers delegate to `launchConsoleFlow`.

Nothing published changes: no export, prop or `packages/i18n` key is added. `flowLaunch.ts` is reachable only through the two handlers. No spec change, and nameless flow buttons are not refused (ruling B, not A).

## Measured before building

The door was read at objectstack origin/main `081e6a09`, which contains `c572fe2a36` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0); the files read were `dispatchFlowAction` and the flow arm of `handleActionsRequest`.

| The handlers read | Where the door's answer carries it |
|---|---|
| transport envelope | `deps.success(result)` / `deps.error(...)`, the same builders as the trigger route (ADR-0112) |
| paused screen: `runId`, `screen`, `flowLabel` | the raw `AutomationResult` as `data`; a paused result is neither a refusal row nor caught by the residual `success === false` arm |
| refused end: `status: 'refused'`, `refusalMessage` | passes through `deps.success` unchanged |
| `successMessage` | unchanged |
| ran and failed | `400` with `error.code` `FLOW_FAILED` and `error.details.errorMessage`, via `FlowActionRefusal` |
| 404 / 409 / 422 / ruling A's 403 | the same shared table and admission rule at both doors |

The door does not carry the flow name. `FlowRunner` resumes under the handler's flow, which on the door path is the declaration's `target`; the lookup requires the two to be equal.

**Related-list row action on a child.** `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.runRowAction` dispatches the child object's declared action with `objectName` set to the child and `recordId` to the child row. At the door that is `POST /api/v1/actions/CHILD/CHILD_ACTION_NAME`. `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` resolves the declaration on the child. `loadActionSubjectRecord` loads the child row under the caller's scope, and `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` answers 404 when that row cannot be read.

**Where the lookup's metadata comes from.** It reads object metadata only. The runtime reads the caller's `objects` first, then the console store's `object` type, awaiting `ensureType('object')` before deciding, as the param dialog already does. The record page reads its `objects` prop. That metadata carries an object's own `actions[]`, which includes every `defineAction({ objectName })`: `defineStack`'s bound-action merge puts them there. The console's list row actions render from `objectDef.actions` alone; `e2e/live/screen-flow.spec.ts` clicks the bound `showcase_bulk_reassign` that way. The metadata does not carry an object-less declared action, nor a standalone authored action row that no object definition embeds. A click on either keeps the trigger route, as every flow click did before, so that is no regression; a pin holds it as a control. No click-time `action` metadata fetch was added.

## Pins

- `useConsoleActionRuntime.flowActionDoor-12037.test.tsx` runs through the real `ConsoleActionRuntimeProvider`, runner and `FlowRunner`:
  - a declared flow action whose `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks is refused by the server with `403` `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and its message is the error toast;
  - control: an allowed click pauses, and Submit resumes at `/api/v1/automation/showcase_reassign_wizard/runs/run-1/resume`, the declaration's target;
  - the store is read (`ensureType('object')`) when the caller holds no objects;
  - an inline button with no name, a dashboard synthesized name, a name whose declaration has another target or type, and an object-less declared action (the control) all stay on the trigger route;
  - an elevated self-triggered target is refused there, and that refusal is the error toast.
- `RecordDetailView.flowActionDoor-12037.test.tsx` runs through the real record page and `FlowRunner`:
  - a related-list row action on the child goes to `/api/v1/actions/lead_task/escalate_task` with `recordId` set to the child row, is refused `403`, and the refusal is shown;
  - the related list's toolbar action sends no parent id, on both doors;
  - control: a header click pauses and resumes under the declaration's target;
  - an undeclared header start stays on the trigger route, where the elevated refusal is shown.

**Reverse leg.** The implementation was committed first (`66291b17c`). The trap-guarded script then checked out main's blobs (`47b1f0bb7`) of the two handler files and ran the two pin files plus the ratchet: `Tests 8 failed | 8 passed (16)`. The 8 failures were every door pin, the two parent-id pins and the delegation pin. The 8 that passed are the trigger-route controls, which hold on main too. After the restore, `git diff HEAD` showed 0 lines, and `git hash-object` equalled the HEAD blob for both files. Re-run on head: `Tests 16 passed (16)`.

## Gates, on head `66291b17c`

- Every suite that mounts either handler, plus FlowRunner's suites, `flowResponse`, the app-shell ratchets, `column-identity.ratchet.test.ts` and `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts`: 84 files. Run with repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run`, under the verify lock, after the final commit: `Test Files 84 passed (84)`, `Tests 596 passed (596)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, gave VERDICT command-exit 0. The upstream closure was built first. `--listFilesOnly` on the test tsconfig lists all four new or edited files.
- `check-changeset-presence` and `check-changeset-no-major` pass. `check:new-line-citations` reports `0 new citation(s)`. `check:control-bytes`, `docs:check-links`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots` and `check-lint-coverage` are all OK.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the 6 touched TS files (count from `--format json`) gives 0 errors. Warnings on the two handler files equal their base blobs: 110 and 38. The repo's `eslint.config.js` has no `projectService` / `parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and the diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict. The full `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are left to CI.

## First-load bytes

Both handlers ship eagerly: the runtime's code is in the eager `DeclaredActionsBar` chunk, and the record page's is in the eager `RecordDetailView` chunk. A console `vite build` under the lock, from `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, gives `eagerGzipBytes` 3,238,611 at base `47b1f0bb7` and 3,238,879 at head: **+268 B gzip**, with 289 eager chunks in both builds.

## Acceptance notes, not changed here

- RecordDetailView's script handler has the same parent-id fallback for a related list's toolbar (its `resolveRecordId` override). It is outside the flow path this PR rewrites, so it is reported only.
- `_rowRecord.id` against `_rowRecord[recordIdField]` was not aligned. The door treats the body's `recordId` as the subject row's primary id and seeds `recordIdParam` from `record[recordIdField]` itself (`seedFlowActionParams`; the spec describes `recordIdField` as "Row field whose value seeds recordIdParam"). So `_rowRecord.id` is the read the door wants. Core's `resolveServerActionRecordId` reads `_rowRecord[recordIdField]` as the record address; the only producer with a non-id `recordIdField` (`sys_session`'s `revoke_session`) is an `api` action that never reaches that reader.
- An object-less declared flow action keeps the trigger route. A nav item does resolve one from `action` metadata, so seeing it would take a new provenance signal or a click-time fetch; neither was added.
- The `packages/app-shell` README has no section on the flow launch, so nothing there became false.

## Surface

The two handler files, the two new pin files, `flow-envelope.ratchet.test.ts`, the docs page and the changeset. One file outside the claim's literal list: the new module-internal `utils/flowLaunch.ts`, the shared call shape (H2) the build round asked to keep module-internal. `ObjectView.tsx` and everything in objectstack are untouched.
